title: Three letters wholly in cipher to Gasparo Spinelli, Venetian resident at Naples, during the Osuna crisis
correspondents: unknown (Venetian senders; Senate, Capi del Consiglio dei Dieci or Inquisitori di Stato likely) → Gasparo Spinelli, Venetian resident at Naples
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Venezia, Archivi propri degli ambasciatori, Napoli, pezzo 7bis (inventory 311 ter, C10)
folio_note: "3 lettere originali completamente in cifra a lui dirette" (20 Oct, 23 Oct 1618 and one more), with loose sheets of Spinelli's residence archive; extent of cipher not given
status: Tiepolo's 1965 inventory (transcribed 2020) lists them as wholly in cipher; no decipherment noted, unlike the Costantinopoli items of the same inventory where 'decifrazione' is stated. Not on DECODE, no repo hit (known.py: Spinelli = only the Florentine Beinecke family). Letters received abroad in Venetian cipher were read by the resident with his own key, so the clear text may survive in the Senate's Deliberazioni (Secreta, Corti/Napoli) or the Capi's registers; the originals themselves are probably not interlined.
why: October 1618 is the height of Venice's quarrel with the viceroy Osuna and the aftermath of the 'Spanish conspiracy'; instructions sent to the Naples resident in full cipher were the most secret part of that correspondence.
score_note: Scored from the archive description during the Oct 2026 Venice archives sweep (research/venice_archives/); not viewed
verify: Order scans of Archivi propri ambasciatori, Napoli 7bis; compare with the Suriano-period residents' cipher (CX, Cifre chiavi e scontri di cifra, b. 1 fol. 3, key a = z10, used 1616-23) and look for the clear text in Senato, Deliberazioni, Secreta (Napoli) and Capi CX lettere, Oct 1618.

title: A 'replica' wholly in cipher among letters from other Venetian ambassadors to Francesco Corner, ambassador in England
correspondents: unknown Venetian diplomat (the bundle holds letters of Giovanni Dolfin, ambassador at Vienna, Lorenzo Tiepolo, ambassador in France, and Pietro Garzoni) → Francesco Corner, Venetian ambassador in London
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Venezia, Archivi propri degli ambasciatori, Inghilterra, pezzo 4 (inventory 311 ter, C6)
folio_note: one letter ('altra «replica» tutta in cifra'), length unknown
status: Inventory: original letters to Corner from Dolfin (Vienna) and Tiepolo (France), 'qualche altra lettera isolata ... altra «replica» tutta in cifra'. No decipherment noted. Not on DECODE, no repo hit (known.py: Corner, Garzoni). Ambassador-to-ambassador letters used a shared Venetian cipher; Corner held the key, so the clear text was probably never filed.
why: Inter-embassy Venetian intelligence during the War of the Spanish Succession (Blenheim and Ramillies years), outside the Senate's despatch series.

title: Senate ducali in cipher to Giovanni Battista Lionello, Venetian resident with the Swiss
correspondents: Doge and Senate of Venice → Giovanni Battista Lionello, Venetian resident in Switzerland (Zurich)
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Venezia, Archivi propri degli ambasciatori, Svizzeri, pezzo 5b (inventory 311 ter, C17); formerly Carte appartenenti a nessun archivio, b. 33
folio_note: original ducali 1620-21 plus 'un gruppo di altre ducali in cifra ... in gran parte duplicate o triplicate'
status: Inventory note 201: group of ducali in cipher, mostly in two or three copies. No decipherment noted. Not on DECODE, no repo hit (known.py: Lionello). The Senate's clear drafts are normally in Senato, Deliberazioni, Secreta (Corti/Svizzeri), so the plaintext very probably survives in Venice: a crib-and-key exercise rather than an unread text.
why: Venetian diplomacy in the Grisons/Valtellina crisis of 1620-21 (Sacro Macello, Spanish occupation of the Valtellina); the duplicates would give clean ciphertext and a key for other 1620s residents' letters.
score_note: Scored from the archive description during the Oct 2026 Venice archives sweep (research/venice_archives/); not viewed
verify: Order scans of Archivi propri ambasciatori, Svizzeri 5b; match against Senato, Deliberazioni, Secreta registers for 1620-21 (Svizzeri); key probably the residents' cipher of CX, Cifre chiavi e scontri di cifra, b. 1-2 (Suriano's key a = z10, 1616-23; the 1621 key a = 156/174, b. 2 fol. 15).

title: Baili at Constantinople to the Capi del Consiglio dei Dieci: selected pages of the Lettere di ambasciatori registers, photographed online
correspondents: Venetian baili at Constantinople → Capi del Consiglio dei Dieci
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Venezia, Capi del Consiglio dei Dieci, Lettere di ambasciatori, Costantinopoli, registers 2-7
folio_note: only pages relevant to the dragomans are imaged (University of Toronto Scarborough, Dragomans / DRRP project); whether any imaged page has cipher is not stated
status: The baili's letters to the Capi were the most secret Venetian despatches and were routinely in cipher with the Secretaries' decipherment filed with them. The UTSC site has page images but its search did not answer for cipher terms, so no cipher page is confirmed. Not on DECODE under this shelfmark (DECODE agent may know more).
why: If imaged pages carry cipher without the decipherment, they are online ciphertext in the Venetian chancery cipher of the 1570s-90s, readable with the Council of Ten's cipher book of 1578-87 (CX, Cifre chiavi e scontri di cifra, b. 4, r. 16).
score_note: Scored from the image site's metadata during the Oct 2026 Venice archives sweep (research/venice_archives/); not viewed
verify: Browse the UTSC images of registers 2-7 for numeric or symbol cipher; keep only pages without the interlined decipherment.
